providers.name: openai
providers.note: Chat Completions. Hosts: OpenAI API (regional us./eu. too), Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry /openai/v1, Bedrock Mantle /v1 and /openai/v1, Bedrock Runtime /openai/v1. `$` keeps the stored-completion endpoints (/chat/completions/{id}) out; /deployments/*/completions is the Azure api-version route.

providers.name: openai
providers.note: Image generation and edits (gpt-image-1). Usage shares input_tokens/output_tokens with the Responses API, so this entry stays before Responses and requires output_tokens_details.image_tokens, which image responses carry and Responses does not. Hosts: OpenAI API only; Azure/Foundry (/openai/deployments/... paths) and Bedrock (/openai/v1) media share hosts with chat and are a follow-up. A streamed image (image_generation.completed, no [DONE]) is not an SSE end marker so its usage is not read yet. input_tokens_details/output_tokens_details carry the per-modality image and text token split.

providers.name: openai
providers.note: Responses API, same hosts as Chat Completions. Usage parsing tries providers in order without a host check and anthropic has the same input/output_tokens keys, so this entry stays before anthropic and requires input_tokens_details. `$` keeps GET /v1/responses/{id} and the unbilled /responses/input_tokens out; /compact is billed. Azure api-version clients post to /openai/responses, or under /deployments/{d}. cached_tokens leaves writes out and input_tokens counts both, so no adding back.

providers.name: openai
providers.note: Audio transcription and translation (gpt-4o-transcribe). The token-usage variant reports usage.type with input_tokens/output_tokens; required_field type keeps it before and apart from anthropic, which has input_tokens/output_tokens but no usage.type. The duration variant (type=duration, seconds, no tokens) has no input_tokens and is skipped here, and a streamed transcription (transcript.text.done, no [DONE]) is not an SSE end marker so its usage is not read yet. Hosts: OpenAI API only; Azure audio (shared host, /openai/deployments/... path) and recording duration-billed or streamed transcription are follow-ups.

providers.name: anthropic
providers.note: Messages. Hosts: Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS, Bedrock Mantle /anthropic/v1, Claude on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed), Claude in Microsoft Foundry /anthropic/v1. `$` keeps /v1/messages/count_tokens and /v1/messages/batches out. Streaming carries speed and inference_geo only in message_start. A server-side fallback response bills each attempt under its own model in usage.iterations; the last entry is the served attempt the top-level usage already counts. A declined attempt that stopped before output bills only when its content fallback block's trigger.category is in billed_categories; its tokens are recorded either way.

providers.name: gemini
providers.note: Hosts: Gemini API, Vertex AI global and {region}-aiplatform, Vertex AI multi-region (us, eu). Path matching is case-sensitive: the streaming method is :streamGenerateContent. URL context and code execution results are billed as input outside promptTokenCount.

providers.name: gemini
providers.note: Gemini Interactions API (POST /v1beta/interactions, also stable /v1); Deep Research runs only through it since 2026-10-08. Same hosts as generateContent. Streaming nests the interaction (with its usage) under `interaction`, unwrapped in the SSE merge; non-streaming carries usage and model at the top level, so one usage_path fits both. total_output_tokens excludes thoughts (docs example 7+23+49=79=total_tokens), so completion is output + thoughts as in generateContent. total_cached_tokens is part of total_input_tokens. required_field keeps this entry off other providers' top-level usage. total_tool_use_tokens is not mapped (its billing relation to input is unconfirmed) and the Vertex interactions:create paths are deferred.

providers.name: anthropic
providers.note: Claude on Vertex AI (global and {region}-aiplatform, multi-region us/eu): Anthropic body, model in the path. `claude-` keeps count-tokens:rawPredict and custom endpoints out.

providers.name: bedrock
providers.note: Bedrock Runtime Converse and InvokeModel. Converse inputTokens leaves out cache tokens; ConverseStream (binary eventstream) has the same usage in its last metadata event. InvokeModel returns the model's own body, so only Anthropic models (read by the anthropic entry) are matched.

providers.name: bedrock
providers.note: Bedrock Runtime InvokeModelWithResponseStream, every model: the last eventstream chunk carries amazon-bedrock-invocationMetrics. Anthropic models are read by the anthropic entry first, from the merged message_start and message_delta usage.
